title: Concerts and Festivals
goal: Find performers and facilities, understand an entry request, and arrange a meeting at a busy event.

runs.text: A
lineup
names the performers at an event. The
headliner
is the main featured act. An
opening act
or
opener
performs before the main act.
Gig
is an informal word for a musician's performance or engagement. A
set
is the group of songs performed during a stretch of the show.
Use this fictional Pine Creek Festival information throughout Practice:

rows.text: Free classical concert at 3 p.m.; no reservation needed
Juniper, the opening band, at 6 p.m.; Northbound, the headliner, at 8 p.m.
Staff inspect bags and check festival wristbands
Glass bottles are not allowed; an empty metal water bottle is allowed
Food trucks beside the main stage; restrooms beside the north gate
Camping area opens Friday at noon; assigned sites have a row letter and number

runs.text: These are this invented festival's conditions. Another event may have different ticketing, entry or camping arrangements.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Who's playing on the main stage tonight?

turns.en: Who's playing on the main stage tonight?

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Juniper at six, then Northbound at eight.

turns.en: Juniper at six, then Northbound at eight.

runs.text: Is Juniper the opener?
Yes.
What time does the headliner start?
asks about the main act, not when the gates open.
Can I see the full lineup?
asks for the wider schedule. For the classical concert,
Do we need to reserve tickets?
checks whether you can simply arrive.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Could you have your bag ready for inspection?

turns.en: Could you have your bag ready for inspection?

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Sure. Is this empty metal bottle okay?

turns.en: Sure. Is this empty metal bottle okay?

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Yes. We don't allow glass bottles.

turns.en: Yes. We don't allow glass bottles.

runs.text: Got it.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Can I see your wristband, please?

turns.en: Can I see your wristband, please?

runs.text: Here it is.
An
inspection
is a check; a
wristband
is a band worn around your wrist, here showing permission to enter.
Could you explain what isn't allowed?
asks for clearer information. A question such as
Can I bring this in?
identifies the actual item rather than assume that every bottle or bag has the same rule.

study.title: Find food, restrooms or a campsite

runs.text: Where are the food trucks?
asks for the food sellers.
Where's the restroom?
asks about toilets.
The line is really long
describes a wait;
Let's try another one
proposes a different option if one is available.

turns.speaker: Camper

runs.text: I can't find my tent. My site is B12.

turns.en: I can't find my tent. My site is B12.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Which row are you in now?

turns.en: Which row are you in now?

runs.text: Row A.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Look for the row B sign. Then follow that row to number twelve.

turns.en: Look for the row B sign. Then follow that row to number twelve.

runs.text: Thanks. Row B, number twelve.

blocks.caption: Find food, restrooms or a campsite · Camper & Staff

runs.text: A
campsite
or
site
here means the assigned place for your tent. Give a useful identifier rather than ask staff to recognize
my tent
without any details.
Is the camping area open yet?
asks about access to that area.
At a crowded event,
I'll meet you later
leaves time and location open. Supply both when you need a definite plan.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: I'm going to the food trucks. Want to come?

turns.en: I'm going to the food trucks. Want to come?

turns.speaker: Riley

runs.text: I'll stay for the rest of this set. Let's meet by the north gate at seven thirty.

turns.en: I'll stay for the rest of this set. Let's meet by the north gate at seven thirty.

turns.speaker: Alex

runs.text: Okay, by the north gate at seven thirty. Then we'll go to the main stage for Northbound.

turns.en: Okay, by the north gate at seven thirty. Then we'll go to the main stage for Northbound.

runs.text: Sounds good.

blocks.caption: Separate and meet again · Alex & Riley

runs.text: If you cannot hear,
It's loud here. Could you text me the meeting place?
requests a different way to receive the information. If delayed,
I'm still in the food line. Can we meet at seven forty-five instead?
proposes a changed time that the other person can accept or reject.
What an amazing performance!
and
That set was great
express enjoyment.
I loved the band, but I couldn't hear the vocals clearly
gives a mixed view.
It was way too loud for me
is a strong personal reaction. There is no requirement to give the same reaction as a companion.
Encore!
calls for another performance after the main performance finishes. An
encore
is that additional performance. A call does not guarantee that the musicians will return.
Speak both roles alone. Use the festival table and the row directions above.
Ask who opens for Northbound and when each band starts. Staff give the schedule. Choose which performance you want to attend.
At entry, staff request your bag and wristband. Ask whether your empty metal bottle is allowed; staff answer from the rule.
Change the item: you have a glass bottle. Ask about it; staff say it cannot come in. Respond
Okay, I won't bring it in
rather than treat the other bottle's permission as applying to it.
You are in row A but your tent site is B12. Ask for help, give the site number, and repeat the direction to check it.

One person wants food; the other stays for the set. Arrange the north-gate meeting at 7:30. Change the response: the food line delays one person. Propose 7:45 and have the other accept or reject it. Support:
That works
That's too late for me; let's keep seven thirty

Hide the models. Ask about the free classical concert's reservation requirement, then reconstruct an entry or meeting exchange. Finish with a positive, negative or mixed reaction to an imagined performance.
Sample possibilities
Who's opening for Northbound? — Juniper, at six. Northbound starts at eight.
Here you go. Can I bring this empty metal bottle in? — Yes.
Okay, I won't bring the glass bottle in.
My site is B12, but I'm in row A. — Look for row B, then number twelve. — Row B, number twelve. Got it.
Can we meet by the north gate at seven thirty?
Later:
I'm delayed. Would seven forty-five work? — Yes, that works.
Do we need to reserve tickets? — No, you can just come.
Reaction:
The band was great, but I couldn't hear the words clearly.
Check:
Did you distinguish gate time from performance time? Did you identify the actual item or campsite? Did the revised meeting have both a place and an agreed time?

note: 入場時刻と演奏時刻は別です。テントの場所や待ち合わせには、目印、番号、時刻をそろえて伝えます。
